endorsements.quote: We recommend that U.S. legislators reach the same conclusion by statute rather than leaving it to litigation, and that physician malpractice liability be extended to chat- 6 bots offering medical guidance.
We recommend that they detect, watermark, and label synthetic health content, and withhold it from wide distribution until experts have vetted it and established its provenance.
Even with such measures in place, users should treat AI-generated health information with caution and consult original sources.

unlisted_practices: AI providers should give users a right of access to their own health interactions with an AI system so they can reconstruct a harmful exchange and show it to a clinician.

AI providers should report, aggregate, and investigate AI health-guidance harms in the same way adverse medical events are, including disclosing how their models handle health queries and which exchanges they flag internally.

Platforms should grant independent researchers direct and ongoing access to deployed AI systems, covering all languages and populations served, with protections specifying who gains access to what data.
AI and search-engine platforms should treat health queries as a distinct, higher-stakes category and answer them only from sources vetted by professional medical societies.
Governments should impose disclosure requirements on AI-generated medical content equivalent to those for pharmaceutical promotion.
U.S. legislators should remove Section 230 immunity for harmful AI-generated health content.

screen.reason: Perspective/commentary outlining risks of generative AI in public health information seeking and offering recommendations for governance, transparency, and harm mitigation.
